overall.sentence: The thesis that overdoped cuprates are Fermi-liquid/BCS d-wave superconductors whose anomalies come from disorder was argued earlier by Lee-Hone, Broun, Hirschfeld and co-workers (arXiv:1802.10198, 1902.08286, cited as [28]-[30]); this Perspective is new chiefly in attributing the anomalies to mesoscopic inhomogeneity rather than effective-medium pair breaking, in the cross-material synthesis (YBCO stiffness, Tl2201 oscillations, Bi2212 gap inversion) and in its falsifiable predictions.

assessment.claim: 1-2: crossover to a weak-coupling BCS/Fermi-liquid overdoped regime, with the anomalies (boomerang, residual C/T and Drude weight, gaps above Tc) extrinsic to disorder
assessment.note: Same question and systems as the earlier dirty d-wave papers [28]-[30]; the method differs (granular, mesoscopic-inhomogeneity picture and a disorder-free phase diagram rather than effective-medium Abrikosov-Gorkov fits), which the paper itself says is an ongoing debate. Search was limited by arXiv rate limits.

assessment.claim: 5: inverting the BCS gap equation on Bi2212 ARPES gives a magnetic-scale pairing interaction that decreases with doping
assessment.note: Valla et al. (2019, not cited) found from ARPES on overdoped Bi2212 that the coupling weakens with doping and vanishes where superconductivity ends, and pointed to spin fluctuations; the gap-equation inversion is a different analysis, so the method facet is new.

assessment.claim: 6: falsifiable predictions for cleaner overdoped cuprates (exponential Tc tail, Ttheta >> Tc, Delta0 ~ 2kBTc, mean-field specific-heat jump, vanishing T-linear resistivity)
assessment.note: Earlier dirty d-wave work implies that cleaner samples should be more BCS-like; the specific list of tests is not found stated there in the abstracts read, but the search was too limited (arXiv refused most queries) to grade no_precedent_found.

positioning: This Perspective sits directly on the line of work by Lee-Hone, Broun, Hirschfeld and co-workers, who argued from 2018 that overdoped LSCO and Tl2201 are compatible with a Landau-BCS description once dopant disorder is treated as dirty d-wave theory; the paper cites these as [28]-[30] but discusses them only in the disorder section and supplementary material, not where it states its proposal. What it adds, as far as the searches show, is the emphasis on mesoscopic inhomogeneity amplified by the short coherence length, the YBCO superfluid-stiffness comparison, the gap-equation inversion of Bi2212 ARPES, and a set of falsifiable predictions; one close uncited ARPES study (Valla et al., arXiv:1905.01370) already reports a pairing coupling that vanishes with overdoping in Bi2212. arXiv refused three of four queries (HTTP 429), so coverage rests on one arXiv query, four web searches and the reference list.

issues.claim: The overdoped regime is BCS/Fermi-liquid-like and its anomalies are extrinsic effects of disorder.
issues.headline: Position the proposal against the earlier dirty d-wave Landau-BCS papers
issues.issue: Lee-Hone, Broun, Hirschfeld and co-workers (arXiv:1802.10198, 1902.08286, 2206.01348; refs [28]-[30]) already argued that overdoped cuprates fit a Landau-BCS picture with disorder explaining the anomalies. The introduction states the proposal without naming this work; it is discussed only later and in the supplement, so a referee may read the headline as claiming more novelty than it has.

evidence.quote: Our primary purpose is to critically assess the validity of a weak-coupling approach to the overdoped cuprates.
evidence.location: Introduction, paragraph after the bullet list

issues.fix: Name refs [28]-[30] where the proposal is stated and say in one clause how this Perspective differs (mesoscopic inhomogeneity versus effective-medium pair breaking; disorder-free phase diagram; predictions).

edit.before: Our primary purpose is to critically assess the validity of a weak-coupling approach to the overdoped cuprates.
edit.after: Our primary purpose is to critically assess the validity of a weak-coupling approach to the overdoped cuprates, building on earlier arguments that dirty d-wave BCS theory accounts for much of the overdoped phenomenology [28-30], from which we differ chiefly in attributing the anomalies to mesoscopic inhomogeneity rather than to homogeneous pair breaking.

issues.claim: Inverting the BCS gap equation on Bi2212 ARPES data gives a magnetic-scale pairing interaction that decreases with doping.
issues.headline: Cite the ARPES study finding vanishing coupling in overdoped Bi2212
issues.issue: Valla, Drozdov and Gu (arXiv:1905.01370, Nat. Commun. 11, 569, 2020) reported from ARPES on overdoped Bi2212 that the coupling weakens with doping and vanishes where superconductivity disappears, and argued for a spin-fluctuation origin. This supports the paper's Fig. 3 conclusion by a different analysis but is not cited.

evidence.quote: Comparing this expectation with direct probes of the doping dependence of the magnetic fluctuations is somewhat complicated.
evidence.location: The nature of the mechanism, paragraph after Fig. 3

issues.fix: Cite Valla et al. as independent ARPES evidence that the pairing coupling in Bi2212 falls with overdoping, and note that the gap-equation inversion reaches the same trend by a different route.

edit.before: Comparing this expectation with direct probes of the doping dependence of the magnetic fluctuations is somewhat complicated.
edit.after: An independent ARPES study of overdoped Bi2212 likewise found that the electron-boson coupling weakens with doping and vanishes where superconductivity disappears [Valla et al., Nat. Commun. 11, 569 (2020)]. Comparing this expectation with direct probes of the doping dependence of the magnetic fluctuations is somewhat complicated.

prior.title: Disappearance of Superconductivity Due to Vanishing Coupling in the Overdoped Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ
prior.overlap: Pairing-relevant coupling in overdoped Bi2212 from ARPES falls to zero with Tc; spin-fluctuation origin proposed.
